data.narrative:
Lumotive is a Series B semiconductor company founded by Gleb Akselrod that has raised $72M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 8 private and 3 public semiconductor firms, including same-stage and adjacent-stage peers such as Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), d-Matrix ($2.0B, Series C), Etched ($5.0B, Series C), and public anchors NVIDIA, AMD, and Analogic.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $72M total raised proxy, yielding $137M. Peer-median analysis across the five same-sector comparables—SambaNova Systems, Etched, d-Matrix, Positron AI, and DEEPX—produces a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range spanning $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied; while the semiconductor sector median P/S multiple is 21.5x across the three public tickers, Lumotive's revenue is not disclosed.

The two applicable methods yield a triangulated range of $116M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.1B. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Lumotive's stage positioning relative to the peer set and the early-stage nature of financial visibility in frontier semiconductor ventures. The peer-median result is most grounded in observable market transactions, though the heterogeneity across stages and valuations within the comp set signals that stage-specific and business-model factors materially drive valuation outcomes in this sector.
